Hi Laura & John - thanks for the details and attachments. High-level answers and recommended approach below; happy to hop on a technical call if helpful.

1) Region pinning model:
- We support tenant-level region pinning: customers can pin a tenant (or route) to a primary region (e.g., us-west-2).
- Failover modes supported: manual failover (operator-initiated) and automated soft failover. Soft failover routes traffic to a secondary region only when health checks indicate primary degraded; requests are tagged and logged so audit trails show cross-region processing.
- Important limitation: automatic cross-region processing requires replicated KV state for in-flight context (KV cache). For low-latency, we recommend warm-standby in a secondary region with continuous async replication of KV snapshots. See attached "region-pinning-limits.csv" for expected replication lag by model size.

2) Backups & residency:
- Snapshot retention: Redwood can store snapshots in a customer-chosen region. For Acme's requirement (US primary, optional EU archival), we can: store primary snapshots in US S3 buckets in your account (recommended), and write an encrypted archival copy to EU only after Legal sign-off.
- Encryption & KMS: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs). If you require keys to remain in the US KMS, we will restrict key creation and storage to the specified KMS region.

3) PII & logging controls:
- Field-level PII: we provide two integration options: (a) customer-side preprocessing (preferred) where you redact/hash fields before sending, or (b) server-side field-level transforms using a transform mapping that runs in your private VPC deployment.
- Audit logs: per-request metadata (tenant, request_id, region, model_version, routed_region) are available and can be pushed to your SIEM via secure forwarding. Logs retained per your retention policy and can be exported to your Log Archive in the region you choose.

4) RTO/RPO / DR design notes:
- With warm-standby + async KV replication we can meet RTO <= 2 hours and RPO <= 1 hour for most medium-size models (<=30B). Larger models will see longer cache-warm times; see replication-lag in attached CSV.
- For strict RTO/RPO at scale we recommend a hybrid approach: (1) warm standby with container image + cached snapshot, and (2) periodic full warm snapshots during business hours to speed startup.

5) Next steps:
- I'll prepare a short architecture diagram and a one-page failover SOP for Acme.
- If you can confirm whether Legal will allow EU archival (even if encrypted & CMK'd in the US), we'll include archival steps in the SOP.
- Proposed: technical PoC week of March 22.
